gp.text: Gross profit. Gross profit for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $11.4 million, compared to $11.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Our gross profit margin was 17.8% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared with 18.1% for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The declines in both gross profit and gross margin for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the prior year period, were isolated to margin pressure with certain industrial customers. These gross profit and margin declines were partially offset by improved gross profit and gross margin across the remainder of our business, where operating initiatives and wallet share expansion continued to take hold.

cor.text: Cost of revenue. Cost of revenue increased $0.5 million, or 1.0%, to $52.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $51.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. This increase in cost of revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily attributable to the higher revenue volumes described above.

oi.text: Our operating results, including revenue, operating expenses, and operating margins, vary from period to period depending on commodity prices of recyclable materials, the volumes and mix of services provided, as well as customer mix during the reporting period, and the timing of acquisitions, divestitures, and impairments.

opex.text: Operating expenses. For the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, operating expenses were $9.7 million and $10.4 million, respectively. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, operating expenses decreased $0.7 million, primarily due to decreases in selling, general and administrative expenses (“SG&A expenses”) and depreciation and amortization of approximately $0.7 million and $0.3 million, respectively, partially offset by a $0.3 million increase in loss on sale of assets.

costs.text: Operating expenses. For the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, operating expenses were $9.7 million and $10.4 million, respectively. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, operating expenses decreased $0.7 million, primarily due to decreases in selling, general and administrative expenses (“SG&A expenses”) and depreciation and amortization of approximately $0.7 million and $0.3 million, respectively, partially offset by a $0.3 million increase in loss on sale of assets.

da_op.text: Operating expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 included depreciation and amortization of $1.0 million and $1.3 million, respectively.

nonint.text: Operating expenses. For the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, operating expenses were $9.7 million and $10.4 million, respectively. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, operating expenses decreased $0.7 million, primarily due to decreases in selling, general and administrative expenses (“SG&A expenses”) and depreciation and amortization of approximately $0.7 million and $0.3 million, respectively, partially offset by a $0.3 million increase in loss on sale of assets.

nonop.text: Interest expense. Interest expense was $2.2 million and $2.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The decrease in expense is primarily due to lower borrowings on our TCB ABL Facility (as defined below) for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to borrowings in the prior year period on our asset-based revolving credit facility with PNC Bank, National Association, successor to BBVA USA (the “PNC ABL Facility”), which was paid in full and terminated effective March 12, 2026..

tax.text: Income taxes. We recorded a provision for income taxes of $38 thousand and $35 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

net.text: Net loss. Net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $(0.5) million, compared to $(1.3) million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The discussions above explain the majority of the changes which contributed to the change in net results year-over-year.

ocf.heading: Cash Flows from Operating Activities
ocf.text:
For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, our net loss of $(15.0) million included a non-cash goodwill impairment loss of $11.0 million and loss on debt extinguishment of $0.5 million. Other non-cash items included in our net loss for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled approximately $6.0 million and related primarily to depreciation, amortization of intangible assets and debt issuance costs and discounts, a provision for doubtful accounts, and stock-based compensation. Net cash provided by the net change in operating assets and liabilities of $1.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was primarily associated with relative changes in accounts receivable, accounts payable, and accrued liabilities.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2025, our net loss of $(13.7) million included a non-cash net loss on sale of $4.3 million and a non-cash intangible asset impairment loss of $1.7 million. Other non-cash items included in our net loss for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 totaled approximately $7.8 million and related primarily to depreciation, amortization of intangible assets and debt issuance costs and discounts, a provision for doubtful accounts, and stock-based compensation.

da.text: Operating expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 included depreciation and amortization of $1.0 million and $1.3 million, respectively.

wc.text: As of September 30, 2026, we had working capital of $9.4 million, including $0.9 million of cash and cash equivalents, compared with working capital of $11.7 million, including $1.0 million of cash and cash equivalents as of December 31, 2025.

Services.text: We are a national provider of waste and recycling management services to customers from across multiple industry sectors that are typically larger, multi-location businesses. We create customer-specific programs and perform the related services for the collection, processing, recycling, disposal, and tracking of waste streams and recyclables to maximize resource utilization. Our programs and services enable our customers to address their business sustainability and environmental, social and governance goals and responsibilities, while also receiving optimized operational efficiencies and lower costs.

intro.text: Quest is a national provider of waste and recycling services that empower larger businesses to excel in achieving their environmental and sustainability goals and responsibilities. Quest delivers focused expertise across multiple industry sectors to build single-source, customer-specific solutions that generate quantifiable business and sustainability results. Addressing a wide variety of waste streams and recyclables, Quest provides information and data that tracks and reports the environmental results of Quest’s services, gives actionable data to improve business operations, and enables Quest’s customers to excel in their business and sustainability responsibilities. For more information, visit https://questrmg.com/ .

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: One customer accounted for 23% and 27% of our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, one of our customers accounted for 23% and 27% of our revenues, respectively.
From year to year, the customers that exceed 10% of our annual revenue, if any, may change.

The following table discloses the number of customers that accounted for more than 10% of our annual revenue and the related receivable balances as of and for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024:

We provide businesses across multiple industry sectors with a single-source, managed services solution for the reuse, recycling, and disposal of a wide variety of waste streams and recyclables generated by their operations.

The industry also includes companies that specialize in certain discrete areas of waste management, operators of alternative disposal facilities, companies that seek to use parts of the waste stream as feedstock for renewable energy and other by-products and waste brokers that rely upon haulers in local markets to address customer needs.
We depend on a small number of customers, and the loss of one or more major customers could have a material adverse effect on our business.
Our ability to expand successfully will depend upon a number of factors, including the following:
Our success in maintaining our existing customers and attracting new customers depends on various factors, including the following:

We rely on independent third-party subcontractors to provide recycling services to our customers, and any interruptions of these arrangements could increase our costs, disrupt our services, and result in our inability to service our recycling customers, which would adversely affect our business.
We rely on our subcontractors to maintain high levels of service.

We rely on third-party service providers to provide services, technology, servers, and hardware for our operations and to maintain our data, and a failure of service by these providers could adversely affect our business and reputation.
We rely upon third-party data center providers to host our primary servers.
We rely on third-party vendors to provide critical services, including, among other things, invoice processing and bill payment services, information technology, and network monitoring.
We depend on these vendors to support our corporate infrastructure and meet our business requirements.

Though we believe that the rates of inflation in recent years have not had a significant impact on our operations, a continued increase in inflation, including inflationary pressure on labor and the goods and services we rely upon to deliver service to our customers, could result in increases to our operating costs, and we may be unable to pass these costs on to our customers.
We depend on key personnel who would be difficult to replace, and our business will likely be harmed if we lose their services or cannot hire additional qualified personnel.
Our success also depends on our ability to attract, retain, and motivate additional skilled management personnel.
Accordingly, investors must rely on sales of shares of their Common Stock after price appreciation, which may never occur, as the only way to realize any return on their investment.

Any future determination as to the declaration and payment of dividends, if any, will be at the discretion of our board of directors and will depend on then existing conditions, including our operating results, financial condition, contractual restrictions, capital requirements, business prospects, and other factors our board of directors may deem relevant.
We derive our primary sources of funds for conducting our business activities from operating revenues; borrowings under our credit facilities; and the placement of our equity securities to investors.

We believe that effective board leadership structure can depend on the experience, skills, and personal interaction between persons in leadership roles as well as the needs of our company at any point in time.
